headline: Saegiru is a shift from older さいぎる, itself from さきぎる (sakigiru), 先 (saki, “in front”) plus 切る (kiru, “cut”).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese verb 老ゆ (oyu).
Development

Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 上(かみ)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (kami nidan katsuyō, “upper bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 上(かみ)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

headline: Yohodo is likely a back-formation from 余っ程 (yoppodo), ultimately from よき (yoki, “good”) plus ほど (hodo, “extent”), with 余 an ateji.

sources.quote: This form is likely a back-formation from from 余(よ)っ程(ぽど) (yoppodo), interpreting the geminated consonant as an intensifier. Ultimately from よき (yoki, “good”) + ほど (hodo, “extent”). The use of the character 余 is an example of ateji (当(あ)て字(じ)).

headline: Kakumei is from Middle Chinese 革命 (“to switch to a new dynasty/regime”), and Fukuzawa Yukichi used it to translate English revolution.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 革命 (MC keak mjaengH, “to switch to a new dynasty/regime”). This word has been used for a long time in Japan, starting from the introduction of I Ching (易經). Fukuzawa Yukichi (福󠄁澤 諭󠄀吉), in Western Affairs (『西洋事情』, 1866–1870), used this word as a translation of the English word "revolution", and it was later popularised by Nakae Chōmin (中江 兆民) and others.
